author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The United States is reviving efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war, with President Donald Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner set to visit Moscow and Kyiv.

Trump says there may be a “good chance” of reaching an agreement, as Washington seeks to restart negotiations after months of stalled diplomacy.

The visit comes as fighting continues to intensify. Ukraine has expanded its strikes inside Russia, while Moscow has responded with frequent attacks on Kyiv and other Ukrainian targets.

Russia currently controls around 20 percent of Ukrainian territory and wants its territorial gains recognised as part of any potential settlement. Ukraine, meanwhile, continues to call for an end to Russia’s occupation and stronger security guarantees.

Witkoff and Kushner previously met Russian and Ukrainian officials in Abu Dhabi. Their latest mission will also take them to Ukraine for the first time, as Kyiv presses Washington to engage more directly with Ukrainian officials.

The diplomat
title: Trump revives Russia-Ukraine peace push as envoys head to Moscow and Kyiv

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The UK has rejected Argentine President Javier Milei’s latest claims over the Falkland Islands, reaffirming its position that the islands remain British.

UK officials, including Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband and Health Secretary Wes Streeting, have stressed that the wishes of the islanders are central to Britain’s position.

The sovereignty dispute between the UK and Argentina dates back centuries. French settlers established a presence on the islands in the 18th century, before Britain took control in 1833. Argentina maintains that the islands were seized by force, while the UK points to the islanders’ right to self-determination.

The dispute led to war in 1982, when Argentina and the UK fought for control of the islands.

Decades later, the sovereignty question remains unresolved, with Argentina continuing to claim the islands, which it calls the Malvinas.

Al Jazeera's Rory Challands reports from London

description:
The United States has sanctioned a Turkish bank as Washington intensifies economic pressure on Iran.

The US Treasury Department accused Golden Global and its subsidiaries of helping Iran transfer oil revenues from China to Turkey. The bank says it has complied with local and international banking rules.

The sanctions are part of the Trump administration’s so-called “Operation Economic Outcast”, aimed at increasing pressure on Iran’s economy.

But how effective can tougher sanctions be? Gulf State Analytics CEO Giorgio Cafiero says the measures could worsen conditions for ordinary Iranians without necessarily achieving Washington’s political objectives.

The discussion also examines how the escalating conflict is changing security calculations across the Gulf. Gulf states are expected to maintain ties with Washington, but some are increasingly looking to diversify their defence and security relationships and become more autonomous from the United States.

Fighting has intensified along the border between Yemen's Taiz and Hodeidah provinces, as Ansarullah Houthi forces and the internationally recognised government battle for control of a strategic stretch of Red Sea coastline.

The Houthis have launched strikes on Taiz, while Saudi-backed government forces say they have shot down drones over Mokha, to the west. Fighting has also spread into Hodeidah. Sources tell Al Jazeera the Houthis are trying to reach and block the road linking Taiz to the port city of Mokha, the main route used to move food, fuel and commercial goods from the Red Sea coast into Yemen. Whoever controls it gains a major foothold over regional transport and supply lines.

The Houthis already hold the capital Sanaa, the northwest and most of the Red Sea coastline, but are pushing to control it entirely. The government controls much of southern and eastern Yemen.

Al Jazeera's Julide Ayger explains.

description: Nine days after devastating Himalayan floods struck Nepal, rescuers have pulled two workers alive from a hydropower tunnel in the hard-hit Rasuwa district, in what has been described as a miraculous development. Local media showed the workers being pulled from the ground before medical teams checked them at the site. There had been no signs of life until the previous day, when a Nepalese lawmaker announced that rescuers had detected survivors. The dramatic breakthrough has raised hopes that more workers could still be trapped inside tunnels at several hydropower projects. Rescue operations remain extremely difficult because of the remote and inaccessible terrain, with the only open land route taking 18 hours from Kathmandu. Helicopters are delivering aid and evacuating the wounded, but damaged infrastructure and the mountainous geography continue to hamper efforts. author: Al Jazeera English
description:
A South African family is refusing to give up hope of finding 33-year-old Terricia Govender, who went missing in Nepal during severe flooding seven days ago. Govender was among a group of pilgrims caught in the disaster, and her mother, Linda, says the family is desperately trying to remain hopeful that she will be found alive. She recalls speaking to her daughter for four hours by video call shortly before she disappeared, as Terricia showed her the clothes and gifts she was planning to bring home. The next morning, Linda received an email from the Isha Sacred Walk informing her of the disaster and immediately feared her daughter was in danger. Despite the uncertainty, she says Terricia is a fighter and insists she will return home. Linda says she wants to travel to Nepal herself and help search for her daughter, while holding on to hope that she is still alive.

The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) is warning that the current El Niño phenomenon could reach exceptional levels, potentially becoming one of the strongest in decades.

WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo says the weather pattern could affect economies and communities across multiple sectors.

Climate specialist Mark Howden explains how El Niño interacts with human-driven climate change and contributes to rising global temperatures and more intense weather extremes.

Southeast Asia, Australia and South America are among the regions facing increased risks of drought, flooding, disrupted agriculture and food insecurity.

The report examines what a stronger El Niño could mean for water resources, food production and communities around the world, as experts call for better preparation, water management and food distribution.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Feminist icon, writer and activist Gloria Steinem has died at the age of 92, leaving behind a decades-long legacy of campaigning for gender equality and social change. From a difficult childhood in Ohio, Steinem went on to study at Smith College and in India, where she drew inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi’s principles of grassroots organising. She rose to national prominence in 1963 after going undercover as a waitress at a Playboy Club and exposing the exploitation of its female workers. She later co-founded Ms. magazine, giving a powerful platform to the growing feminist movement and issues including domestic violence, equal pay and maternity leave. Steinem also helped establish organisations supporting women in politics and remained a prominent activist, including at the Women’s March following Donald Trump’s election in 2016. She continued speaking out on reproductive rights and sexual harassment, and was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2013. 

Al Jazeera’s Patty Culh
title: Gloria Steinem, trailblazing feminist and activist, dies at 92

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
With US midterm elections looming and oil prices hovering at around $97 a barrel, questions remain over Washington's strategy in the Strait of Hormuz and its conflict with Iran. 
In an interview with Al Jazeera, Trita Parsi of the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft said the US is "overstating" its success in stabilising shipping through the Strait, while acknowledging that US escorts are helping more vessels pass through. 
He warned Iran may seek to trigger conflict before the midterms to damage President Donald Trump politically, but said a "humiliated" Trump after the elections could become "much more desperate and reckless", increasing the risk of further escalation. Parsi also said China is pursuing its own interests by reducing oil demand to help prevent a global recession, rather than assisting the US against Iran, and argued that both sides are "overstating the degree to which they are getting support."
